meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic, modified by EU harmonized corporate and AML/CFT law; SCSp is a civil-law limited partnership with common-law partnership characteristics)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties with 90+ third states, in force
Luxembourg income and capital tax treaties with 80+ jurisdictions, including the Luxembourg-United States DTA in force
EU free trade agreements and the European Economic Area Agreement applicable to Luxembourg
OECD/G20 Multilateral Convention on Implementing Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Loi du 13 janvier 2019 portant création d'un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2018 on the organisation of the RCS and the Luxembourg Business Registers; EU Directives AMLD4, AMLD5 and AMLD6, as implemented in Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport authority of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 Hague Convention, or consular legalization if country of issue is not a Hague member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign corporate register extract or certificate of incumbency of any corporate general partner or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies House or equivalent competent registry of the corporate entity's place of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions; if in a language other than French, German, English or Luxembourgish, accompanied by certified translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Luxembourg registered agent and filing counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of residence of the general partner or the person signing on behalf of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the constitutive documents and proof of good standing of the foreign general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or competent governmental authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill, bank statement or equivalent issued within the last three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank or municipal authority of the UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of issuance and, where required by local law or the Luxembourg filing agent, Hague Apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, general partners, managers and authorized signatories against the PEP list of the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council Sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, and the Luxembourg national sanctions register. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons, high-risk third-country nationals, and persons controlled by such individuals. The appointed domiciliation agent and any Luxembourg chartered accountant or law firm retained for the SCSp are obliged entities under the Luxembourg AML law and will apply risk-based CDD, source of wealth review, ongoing monitoring and filing of suspicious transaction reports.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), available at lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed names must be submitted in the Latin alphabet and must comply with Luxembourg's official linguistic framework (French, German and Luxembourgish). A name in a non-Latin script or in a foreign language is accepted only if transliterated and, if required by the registrar, accompanied by a certified French or German translation. The statutory suffix indicating the legal form, 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale', is mandatory and must appear in the full legal name. Names must be distinguishable from existing registrations, must not mislead the public, and must not contravene public policy or bonos mores.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar refuses a proposed name, the applicant may first request an internal reconsideration through the LBR helpdesk, specifying the grounds for name availability and submitting corrected documentation. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, an administrative annulment appeal may be filed before the Tribunal administratif by a lawyer admitted to the Luxembourg Bar. The appeal must be introduced within the statutory deadline under Luxembourg administrative procedure, normally three months from notification of the refusal, and must set out the reasons for annulment. The contested name remains unavailable during the appeal unless the tribunal grants a temporary suspension. In cases of ministerial prior authorization for sensitive tokens, the refusal may be remedied by obtaining the required authorization from the Ministry of Justice, the CSSF or another competent ministry before resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The SCSp must maintain a registered office in Luxembourg. A pure 'virtual office' without a physical Luxembourg address is not permissible as the statutory registered office. The SCSp may use the address of a licensed professional domiciliation company that provides physical registered office services, administrative capacity and access to corporate records. Remote back-office and fulfillment operations for the online retail of consumer electronics are commercially permissible, provided the registered office address remains a real, accessible address capable of receiving service of process and official communications.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-Medium. For a low-risk, non-licensed e-commerce SCSp domiciled with a regulated Luxembourg domiciliation provider, the annual likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection is approximately 12%. The likelihood rises to approximately 30% if the domiciliation agent is subject to regulatory review, the SCSp is selected by the RCS for a compliance sample, or adverse media or sanctions hits are identified.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the SCSp; Articles 25-1 to 25-7 and general provisions applicable to commercial companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: RCS initial registration application (demande d'inscription au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) together with the executed partnership agreement and annexes, including registered-office consent, manager acceptance and UBO declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital. Partners may contribute cash or in kind; contributions need not be paid up at formation unless the partnership agreement so requires. No escrow or capital blocking account is mandated by Luxembourg company law; a bank deposit verification may be required to evidence cash contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST FORMATION RESOLUTION (GENERAL PARTNER ACTION IN LIEU OF A BOARD): RESOLVED, that the undersigned general partner of the SCSp hereby approves the formation of the Société en Commandite Spéciale under the amended Law of 10 August 1915; adopts the executed partnership agreement as the charter; authorizes the subscription by the partners of their respective partnership interests set forth therein; adopts the registered office at [address]; appoints [Name] as manager/administrator with full powers to execute filings and open bank accounts; and ratifies all pre-formation acts done in the company's name. This resolution is effective immediately upon execution and shall be recorded in the company's minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability verification and formation-pack preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), RCS online portal at lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the proposed name '[Target Name] SCSp' through the RCS online name search. The name must include 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale', must be distinctive and non-misleading. If available, prepare the SCSp partnership agreement, registered-office consent letter, manager acceptance and ultimate beneficial owner declaration.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and legal form suffix
Identification details of all general partners and limited partners
Declaration of the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the name for similarity, file a reasoned response or select a new distinctive name; final name refusal is curable by amending the partnership agreement and resubmitting the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarisation of statutory formation instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary for notarial deed scenarios, otherwise the partners under private signature; drafting must comply with the Law of 10 August 1915.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have the general partner and limited partners execute the partnership agreement either by private deed with certified signatures or before a Luxembourg notary if the contribution comprises Luxembourg real estate. The agreement must state the corporate name, registered office, purpose covering online retail of consumer electronics and smart gadgets, duration, capital and contribution rules, transfer provisions and management powers. Attach the registered-office consent, manager acceptance and any power of attorney. For private agreements, use qualified electronic signatures or hand-signed counterparts.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (statuts or convention de société)
Registered-office consent letter from landlord or service provider
Written acceptance of appointment by each manager
Power of attorney, if filing agent is appointed
Contribution-in-kind report by a statutory auditor, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the RCS detects a defect in the deed, execute an amending act and re-file; if the contribution-in-kind report is missing, fund the contribution in cash and provide the corresponding bank certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription and opening of a Luxembourg bank or client account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or payment/e-money institution supervised by the CSSF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a licensed Luxembourg bank or payment institution and submit the executed formation documents and AML/KYC forms. The partners must subscribe their partnership interests; if a target capital is set, each partner transfers the agreed cash contribution to the SCSp's dedicated account. The bank issues an account opening document and confirmation of paid-in amounts. The SCSp has no legal minimum capital, but contractual contribution commitments must be honoured.
required_dossiers: AML/KYC forms and beneficial-ownership declaration under the Law of 13 January 2019
Identity and proof of address of each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays KYC approval, provide a clear beneficial-ownership chart and source-of-funds documentation; if the bank refuses on substance concerns, submit evidence of a Luxembourg registered office, local management and a concrete e-commerce business plan.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS e-filing of the formation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés e-filing module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RCS initial registration form via the LBR online portal. Attach the executed partnership agreement, acceptance of appointment, registered-office consent and UBO declaration. The applicant or notary signs the application and pays the prescribed state fee. The RCS reviews the filing against the Law of 10 August 1915 and transparency requirements. Upon approval, the RCS assigns the registration number; for an SCSp this registration provides publicity and evidentiary effects but does not by itself create legal personality unless the partnership elects otherwise.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement or notarial deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a formal deficiency notice, correct and resubmit the documents within fifteen days; if the business purpose is deemed too broad, narrow the statutory purpose clause to ISIC 4791 online retail activities and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA publication, post-registration extract and follow-on registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the registry publishes a formation extract in RESA. Verify that the publication accurately states the name, registered office, managers and purpose. Obtain the official RCS excerpt and then proceed with post-formation registrations: VAT identification with the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, social security registration with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale, and the establishment-authorisation application with the Ministry of the Economy if commercial activity is commenced.
required_dossiers: Business establishment authorisation application, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication contains errors, request a rectification from the RCS using the amending-form process; if VAT or social security registration is delayed, provide the RCS excerpt through the relevant portal and escalate to the competent administrations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy of Luxembourg (Ministère de l'Économie) - Business Establishment Service / Guichet unique for establishment permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) under the Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to commercial, craft and industrial professions

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA report; pure online retail of consumer electronics is not an EIA-listed project under Luxembourg EIA legislation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission thresholds are triggered for pure e-commerce retail. Any office or warehouse must comply with general municipal waste-sorting rules, packaging-waste obligations and the WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU for electronics placed on the market.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours, structural load and occupancy clearance from the competent municipal authority, and occupational health clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines before employees occupy commercial premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income tax, municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT (TVA); Customs and Excise Agency (ADA) for export procedures. Single e-filing entry through MyGuichet.lu (guichet.public.lu); direct-tax portal at impotsdirects.public.lu; VAT/AEDT portal at aed.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Register the SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale under the law of 23 July 2016) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu; the RCS registration triggers issuance of the national business register number and the ACD tax reference (numero de matricule). 2. Submit the fiscal declaration form 710 to ACD; the fiscally transparent SCSp obtains its own matricule for direct tax declarations of allocable income. 3. Register for VAT with AEDT using form 563 (available on MyGuichet.lu) to obtain a Luxembourg VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits). 4. Enrol in the Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme on the AEDT portal for B2C distance sales of electronic gadgets destined to other EU member states. 5. Register for an EORI (LU + 12 digits) with the Customs and Excise Agency to lodge export declarations for third-country consignments, using Stripe/PayPal settlement records as ancillary proof of revenue booking.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime exists in Luxembourg; the SCSp is mandatorily fiscally transparent, meaning it has no separate taxable personality for income tax, net wealth tax, or VAT and each partner is taxed directly on their allocable share. The general partner may lawfully allocate the VAT-taxable e-commerce activity to the partnership's permanent establishment and is treated as the taxable person for VAT compliance. No hybrid mismatch election is available domestically, but taxpayers must file an annual disclosure with ACD for any cross-border arrangements exploiting hybrid entities or instruments within the meaning of the ATAD II implementing law of 21 December 2018 and 20 December 2019; a fiscally transparent SCSp may be subject to symmetrical treatment alignment by treaty where the partner's residence state regards it as opaque.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law (Loi modifiée du 12 février 1979 relative à la TVA) and EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-business exemption (art. 145(2) Loi TVA); for distance sales of consumer electronics to EU end consumers, an EU-wide EUR 10,000 annual threshold applies, above which Luxembourg VAT registration for OSS is replaced by destination-state VAT via the Union OSS quarterly return; a non-established foreign seller has no registration threshold and must register in Luxembourg whenever a taxable supply occurs in the territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API tax-stamping, or digital stamping regime exists in Luxembourg. B2B/B2C e-invoices must conform to EU VAT invoice rules (issuance within 15 days, sequential numbering, supplier/buyer identification, taxable amount, VAT rate and amount). Mandatory structured e-invoicing applies exclusively to B2G invoices addressed to Luxembourg public-sector bodies, which must be exchanged through the Peppol network in UBL/CIUS format. For online payments via Stripe and PayPal, the exporter must retain the complete payment reconciliation trail linking each transaction to the export proof; Manco/Data-related e-archiving must be kept for 6 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically dispatched from Luxembourg to destinations outside the EU are zero-rated under art. 53 Loi TVA provided export is evidenced by customs documentation and the goods leave the EU within 90 days of supply. Intra-community supplies to EU-registered taxable persons are zero-rated under art. 54 Loi TVA when the recipient's valid VAT number is confirmed by VIES and the goods are dispatched to another member state; the exemption is subject to recapitulative statement (EC Sales List) and Intrastat filing. B2B electronic services and software hosting supplied to an EU business established outside Luxembourg or to B2C customers outside the EU qualify for 0% under the place-of-supply rules of arts. 42-44 Loi TVA, with the place of establishment of the customer determining territoriality.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD - Document Administratif Unique) with the resulting Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note or courier delivery scan evidencing physical exit from the EU
Commercial invoice stating Incoterms, HS codes (e.g., 8471, 8517, 8543) and export reason
Payment proof and booked inward remittance (Stripe/PayPal settlement report or bank confirmation) evidencing that proceeds were credited to the Luxembourg account within the allowed period
European Community Sales List (EC Sales List) and Intrastat declarations for intra-EU zero-rated dispatches
OSS quarterly VAT return (VAT 500/503) where distance sales are taxed at the destination state
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT may retroactively claw back the 17% VAT not properly zero-rated, plus default interest of 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum) and a 10% late-payment surcharge (droit en sus, art. 84 Loi TVA) if export documentation is missing or fraudulent. Administrative fines range from EUR 250 to EUR 250,000, augmentable to twice the tax evaded for intentional concealment, and criminal sanctions provide imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years (arts. 80-83 Loi TVA). The reclamation window is 5 years from the end of the year in which the return was filed, extended to 10 years for offences committed with fraudulent intent; retroactive OSS-denial at the rate of the destination member state may also be imposed where the dispatch proof does not meet the substantive requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the prudential and AML/KYC banking supervisory authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg, as an EU/EMU member state, applies full current and capital account convertibility with the euro as legal tender. There are no exchange controls, approval requirements, or restrictions on the repatriation of profits, dividends, capital contributions, or loan repayments. Cross-border conversion between EUR, USD, CNY, and other freely traded currencies is conducted at commercial bank market rates. The only practical constraints are standard bank AML/KYC due diligence, tax reporting formalities, and the requirement that the SCSp maintain demonstrable economic substance and proper accounting records. Profit distributions from the SCSp are governed by the partnership agreement and follow the tax-transparent character of the structure, with no Luxembourg exchange-control permission required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg does not impose mandatory surrender, repatriation timelines, or minimum conversion ratios for export proceeds. Receivables from online consumer-electronics retail sales may be retained in EUR or foreign currency and converted freely through Luxembourg banks. Banks remain obliged to report monetary statistics to the BCL for balance-of-payments purposes and to apply standard AML surveillance, but no statutory conversion or surrender obligation is triggered.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Multi-Currency Operational Account
Operational Account / Trade Finance Account / Escrow Structure
Operational Account / Multi-Currency Settlement and Merchant Acquiring Account
Operational Account / Digital Banking Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate-to-High as a complementary payment layer, but Low as the sole treasury infrastructure. A CSSF-licensed electronic money institution (EMI) or an EEA-passported EMI may lawfully hold merchant funds, provide multi-currency IBANs, and execute FX conversion; however, an EMI is not a credit institution and cannot offer deposit protection, documentary letters of credit, committed credit lines, or full treasury safeguarding. Stripe and PayPal operate as payment service providers or merchant-of-record processors rather than principal Luxembourg banks; they may settle consumer-electronics sales but should not be treated as the primary bank relationship. The SCSp should maintain at least one principal regulated Luxembourg credit institution account for capital escrow, trade settlements, and regulatory credibility. Legal constraints include the EMD2 safeguarding regime, client-money separation, CSSF AML/KYC obligations, and the fact that an EMI cannot execute commercial bank instruments such as SWIFT-backed commercial letters of credit.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for at least one authorised signatory and typically for the managing partner or general partner of the SCSp during initial onboarding. Most Luxembourg banks mandate an in-person interview at the bank's premises for the beneficial owners or controlling partners, particularly where the SCSp is owned by non-resident individuals or through an intermediate holding chain. Remote video onboarding is permitted by some Luxembourg banks on a risk-based basis, but only after enhanced due diligence, notarised identity documentation, apostilled corporate documents, and satisfactory source-of-funds evidence. It is prudent to assume that a physical interview may be required unless the bank explicitly confirms remote opening. The SCSp must provide its partnership agreement, a valid power of attorney if applicable, identification and proof of address for the general partner and ultimate beneficial owners, and a clear commercial explanation for the cross-border retail treasury flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed or opaque beneficial-ownership layers above the SCSp, including foreign limited partnerships or nominee arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate and ownership chain chart down to natural persons; notarised and apostilled constitutional documents; self-certification of ultimate beneficial ownership; Luxembourg UBO register reflection where applicable; audited or management financial statements of each material investor; source-of-wealth documentation; and written confirmation that no nominee, trustee, or bearer-share arrangement exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SCSp is a zero-minimum-capital pass-through partnership, which can raise risk of unexplained capital contributions or phantom funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully signed and notarised partnership agreement; capital account ledger with date, amount, and remitter for each contribution; bank MT103 remittance records matching capital account entries; independent valuation of any in-kind contribution; investor know-your-customer files; tax identification numbers of all partners; and a board or manager resolution approving each capital inflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border consumer-electronics e-commerce with third-party payment processors, chargebacks, refunds, and potential commingling of retail proceeds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe and PayPal merchant settlement statements; processor monthly reconciliation reports; chargeback and refund policy documentation; customer order history with logistics and shipment evidence; supplier purchase invoices; inventory records; ecommerce platform contractual terms; and independently prepared management accounts showing the flow of funds from retail sales to the Luxembourg bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments involving higher-risk jurisdictions, non-face-to-face onboarding, or counterparties with no apparent economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP screening results for all counterparties; country risk assessment; tax-residency certificates of counterparties and beneficial owners; commercial rationale for the jurisdiction of suppliers and customers; evidence of Luxembourg economic substance such as registered office, physical or administrative presence, local banking activity, and records maintained in Luxembourg; and a written AML compliance manual adopted by the SCSp.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital contributions to the SCSp must be routed through a regulated Luxembourg credit institution using the SWIFT MT103 message standard for non-EEA investors or SEPA credit transfer for EEA investors. The remittance instruction must carry the SCSp legal name, the reference to the executed partnership agreement and capital account, and a payment purpose narrative such as 'Capital Contribution to SCSp'. The receiving bank will typically require completion of its external-settlement questionnaire and a balance-of-payments reporting declaration to the BCL. Funds must be fully cleared and pass bank compliance before they are released to the operational treasury. For larger or institutional commitments, an escrow-capable account under a segregated internal ledger is recommended. The bank must also verify that the remitter is the identified investor and that no third-party funding occurs unless a fully documented assignment or contribution agreement is provided.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for procurement of consumer electronics should use SWIFT MT103 for direct open-account supplier payments and SWIFT MT202 COV for correspondent-bank cover where required. Commercial documentary letters of credit (UCP600, typically issued via SWIFT MT700/MT710) provide secured settlement for larger or recurring supplier purchases. Bills for collection under URC522 remain permissible but are less common for consumer-electronics retail. Retail disbursements are settled through Stripe and PayPal merchant acquiring flows, with net proceeds converted to EUR or USD in the Luxembourg operational account. All outbound MT103 messages must include a purpose code mapped to trade in goods, supplier invoice numbers, and product category references so that the correspondent bank and clearing systems can process the payment without AML delays. Cash pooling across EU subsidiaries should be executed via SEPA Instant Credit Transfer where applicable, with SWIFT GPI tracking for non-EEA payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNH, EUR/GBP) executed with the Luxembourg principal bank or an investment-grade counterparty
FX swaps for rolling short-term liquidity and settling mismatched receivables/payables
Cross-currency swaps for longer-duration balance-sheet hedging between EUR and retail procurement currencies
Plain-vanilla FX options (call/put) for budgeted downside protection on key currency pairs
Non-deliverable forwards only for restricted or less-convertible currencies that do not have a developed onshore deliverable market, subject to EMIR reporting and board-approved treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, annexes) deposited with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); SCSp is subject to the accounting-records regime of the Law of 19 December 2002
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the eJustice.lu portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the close of the financial year (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end); a single one-month extension may be requested from the RCS prior to expiry of the initial deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent non-filing triggers an LBR penalty notice (commonly EUR 250 per document); the general partner (gérant) faces criminal fines under the Law of 19 December 2002; the Tribunal de Commerce may order dissolution and administrative strike-off of the SCSp in cases of manifest and continued default

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO declaration and update filings (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) with the RCS beneficial-owner register, reconciled annually with the register of limited partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) / Luxembourg Business Registers via the eJustice.lu UBO portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing within 30 days of RCS registration; any change in beneficial ownership (transfer of partnership interests, admission or retirement of limited partners, change of control in the general partner) must be filed within 30 days; annual accuracy review is performed in conjunction with the RCS annual-accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under the Law of 13 January 2019: up to EUR 1,250 for unjustified non-filing and up to EUR 1,250,000 in aggravated intentional cases, with publication of sanctions; inaccurate or incomplete declarations block subsequent RCS filings and may trigger court-imposed periodic penalty payments (astreintes)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual direct tax filings: corporate income tax and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, ICC), accompanied by an informational pass-through schedule allocating profits to the partners of the fiscally transparent SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - competent bureau d'imposition, via the eCDF electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months of the close of the financial year (31 May for a 31 December year-end); extensions may be granted by the ACD upon reasoned request filed in eCDF before the legal deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file allows the ACD to proceed with estimated taxation (taxation d'office) with a 10% surcharge; late-payment interest accrues on assessed amounts; the general partner may incur a late-filing penalty and criminal fines in cases of willful default, while intentional omission may jeopardize the SCSp's tax-transparency treatment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT declaration and EU recapitulative statement / annual client listing for cross-border B2B supplies of consumer electronics
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - Luxembourg VAT division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual client listing and VAT annexes due by 30 April of the calendar year following the reporting year; periodic VAT returns (monthly or quarterly, depending on turnover) due by the 15th day of the following month or quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missing VAT returns attract administrative fines (typically EUR 50-500 per return) plus statutory default interest; failure to file the recapitulative statement suspends the exercise of intra-EU VAT deduction rights and may trigger cross-border EU penalty notification procedures

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by an ILRE-registered independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) is compulsory if the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: (a) total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million; (b) net turnover EUR 8.8 million; (c) average workforce of 50 employees. An audit is also mandatory where the partnership agreement so requires, where the SCSp forms part of a consolidated group filing consolidated accounts, or where the entity operates as a regulated professional of the financial sector (PFS) or investment-fund vehicle.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on accounting records (transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU), including the Plan comptable normalisé luxembourgeois; IFRS as endorsed by the European Union is optional for the statutory accounts of unlisted entities and mandatory for consolidated accounts where the group adopts IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg applies a continuous-disclosure UBO regime without a standalone annual UBO form: the SCSp must file the initial UBO declaration within 30 days of RCS registration and file corrective updates within 30 days of any change in the register of limited partners, transfer of partnership interests, admission or retirement of partners, or change of control in the general partner. The annual compliance protocol requires the general partner to certify, at each RCS annual-accounts filing, that the UBO entries on the eJustice.lu portal remain accurate and complete; if a partnership-interest transfer occurred during the year, the corrective UBO declaration must be validated before or simultaneously with the annual-accounts deposit. Persistent inaccuracy of the UBO file blocks subsequent statutory filings (annual accounts, notarized deeds) and carries the sanctions listed in the compliance matrix.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners with their capital contributions and transfer records (kept by the general partner at the registered office)
Register of Managers/Gérants and their powers of representation
Minute Book (procès-verbaux) of partner meetings and management decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200-3,500 per year (EUR 1,100-3,200), depending on corporate secretarial scope, registered-office location, and AML/KYC file maintenance for the general partner and limited partners
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500-14,000 per year (EUR 4,200-13,000), for a certified statutory audit of a mid-size online consumer-electronics retailer with high transaction throughput, quoted by ILRE-registered audit firms

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate headline CIT rate for a Luxembourg City-resident taxable company (17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge on the CIT, and 6.75% municipal business tax; the municipal rate varies by commune). An SCSp is fiscally transparent and is generally not subject to entity-level CIT.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday is available to a Luxembourg SCSp as such. Income is taxed at the level of the partners. Preferential deductions include the 80% exemption for qualifying IP income under Luxembourg's IP regime, the participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains available to corporate partners, and the availability of treaty/foreign tax credits at partner level.
